Since \(x=3\) and \(y=2-\sqrt3\), we have
\[
\frac1y=\frac1{2-\sqrt3}=2+\sqrt3.
\]
Thus
\[
y+\frac1y=(2-\sqrt3)+(2+\sqrt3)=4.
\]
So
\[
y^3+\frac1{y^3}=\left(y+\frac1y\right)^3-3\left(y+\frac1y\right)=4^3-3(4)=64-12=52.
\]
Also,
\[
2x^3=2(3^3)=54.
\]
Therefore,
\[
2x^3-\left(y^3+\frac1{y^3}\right)=54-52=2.
\]
\[
\boxed{2}
\]
